author_or_org: Ling Wang, Xin Liu, Songnan Liu, Jianan Wang, Cheng Cheng, Yihan Zhu, Enyu Li, Yu Xiao, Jiangyong Xie, Duogong Yan, Jiangyi Chen

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: HEAR is an enterprise agentic reasoner built on a Stratified Hypergraph Ontology, with a base Graph Layer that virtualizes provenance-aware data interfaces and a Hyperedge Layer that encodes n-ary business rules and procedural protocols.
claims.quote: We introduce HEAR, an enterprise agentic reasoner built on a Stratified Hypergraph Ontology. Its base Graph Layer virtualizes provenance-aware data interfaces, while the Hyperedge Layer encodes n-ary business rules and procedural protocols.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Applying LLMs to heterogeneous enterprise systems is said to be hindered by hallucinations and failures in multi-hop, n-ary reasoning.
claims.quote: Applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to heterogeneous enterprise systems is hindered by hallucinations and failures in multi-hop, n-ary reasoning.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Existing paradigms such as GraphRAG and NL2SQL are said to lack the semantic grounding and auditable execution required for complex enterprise environments.
claims.quote: Existing paradigms (e.g., GraphRAG, NL2SQL) lack the semantic grounding and auditable execution required for these complex environments.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: HEAR operates an evidence-driven reasoning loop and dynamically orchestrates ontology tools for structured multi-hop analysis without requiring LLM retraining.
claims.quote: Operating an evidence-driven reasoning loop, HEAR dynamically orchestrates ontology tools for structured multi-hop analysis without requiring LLM retraining.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: On supply-chain tasks, including order fulfillment blockage root cause analysis, HEAR achieves up to 94.7% accuracy.
claims.quote: Evaluations on supply-chain tasks, including order fulfillment blockage root cause analysis (RCA), show HEAR achieves up to 94.7% accuracy.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: HEAR uses procedural hyperedges to minimize token costs and leverages topological exploration for rigorous correctness on complex queries.
claims.quote: Crucially, HEAR demonstrates adaptive efficiency: utilizing procedural hyperedges to minimize token costs, while leveraging topological exploration for rigorous correctness on complex queries.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: HEAR matches proprietary model performance with open-weight backbones and automates manual diagnostics.
claims.quote: By matching proprietary model performance with open-weight backbones and automating manual diagnostics, HEAR establishes a scalable, auditable foundation for enterprise intelligence.
